name: Dating
intro: Where the people on the other side are real and chats go somewhere, and where it is empty profiles and bots.

apps.title: My Love - Relationship Counter
apps.verdict: A simple, accurate relationship counter that does exactly what it's designed for. Couples genuinely love it.
apps.loved: The home-screen widget shows the counter in real time, and anniversary and special-date reminders fire reliably.
apps.weak: The rating prompt pops up on every launch and covers the screen on special days, making it hard to take a screenshot.
apps.whoFor: Couples who want to track the history of their relationship.

I personally love this app because I can finally keep up with my relationships. Anything that I don’t like is that I can only have 1 relationship on there. Also I feel that Love pro shouldn’t be a thing and that it should be free. Otherwise

apps.title: Between, Couples Love Tracker
apps.verdict: A private space for two with a shared memory vault, used by couples for years, but a serious incident of irreversible loss of thousands of photos undermines trust.
apps.loved: The feeling of a world that belongs only to the two of you, storing photos and messages in one place for years. Stickers and themes make conversations feel warmer.
apps.weak: Several serious incidents where thousands of photos were permanently lost after crashes, with no recovery and no response from the company. New features appear very rarely.
apps.whoFor: Couples, especially long-distance ones, who want a personal digital space separate from regular messaging apps.

quotes.text: I will answer your question of "why only one star?" In just a moment. First off I have to say that my partner and I were looking for an app that did exactly what this one does. We tried several apps and this was the one. Loved all of the fe

I've used Between with my partner for over 8 years. It was so fun in the beginning with the stickers and occasional celebration free stickers (who remembers the corgi?). But now I feel like there's nothing for the app to offer. The lack of

My girlfriend and I used this app about six years ago…but then something happened and we broke up…now, all these years later we are together again and we were reminiscing about our past and all the wonderful memories….this app came up in ou

apps.title: Evergreen: Relationship Growth
apps.verdict: An app for couples rather than for finding a partner. Daily questions, quizzes, and mini-lessons help deepen a relationship. Especially valued in long-term and long-distance relationships. The main flaw is that content runs out faster than users expect.
apps.loved: Daily questions open up topics the couple would never have raised on their own. Several users say a partner who used to avoid serious conversations started opening up through the app's game-like format.
apps.weak: Questions start repeating after one or two months of active use. Accumulated points have nothing to spend them on, which is frustrating. There is no built-in chat for discussing answers.
apps.whoFor: Couples in long-term or long-distance relationships who want a structured way to talk about more than just how the day went.

apps.title: Cozy Couples: Relationship App
apps.verdict: A private couple space with a shared cat, a daily question, and a mood widget. Works as a ritual of presence in long-distance relationships.
apps.loved: A daily question with the partner's answer visible, a mood widget on the lock screen, and joint care for a virtual cat as a simple shared ritual.
apps.weak: After a few months things feel stagnant due to infrequent updates. The game selection does not expand, and the app is useless if one partner stops logging in.
apps.whoFor: Long-distance couples who need a daily connection ritual beyond texting.

quotes.text: My gf and I downloaded this at the beginning of January, and it has helped our connection 1000%. There is a cat and a plant to take care of together, as well as games to play and prompts to answer like, "what is one thing you love about y

apps.title: SumOne: For Relationships
apps.verdict: A companion app for couples with daily questions and a shared virtual pet. Not about finding someone new but about staying connected with an existing partner. Users return for hundreds of days in a row, especially in long-distance relationships.
apps.loved: A daily question whose answer stays hidden until the partner answers too, creating an honest mutual-disclosure mechanic. The Eggmon pet, cared for together, builds attachment to the app.
apps.weak: After several months questions become repetitive or turn negative. Earning the in-app currency (pebbles) is too slow. The app does not work if the partner is gone. The account is not designed for solo use.
apps.whoFor: Couples, especially in long-distance relationships or at the early stages of getting to know each other, who want to maintain emotional closeness through structured dialogue.

quotes.text: We've been using this for almost 500 days now and I still love it dearly. You raise a cute creature that supposedly changes what they turn out to be out of a choice of 4 different ones by answering questions with your partner, how long your

apps.title: Paired: Couples & Relationship
apps.verdict: Paired solves a real problem: keeping a living dialogue in a couple through daily questions and games. Users in multi-year relationships report gaining closeness. The weak point is too much sexual content and too few tools for handling conflict.
apps.loved: Daily questions open up topics couples have avoided for years, especially valuable in long-distance relationships.
apps.weak: A tilt toward sexual topics. If one partner stops participating the app becomes useless.
apps.whoFor: Couples who want to talk more deeply, especially in long-distance relationships or during a rut.

quotes.text: My husband got this for us because we've always been #goals but we were drifting & past resentments or unmet needs were building this silent, invisible wall we could feel keeping us fully present even if snuggled up. So, we went in without

apps.title: Couple Joy - Relationship App
apps.verdict: Daily themed questions spark conversations the couple would not normally get to, and this genuinely works as a tool for deepening dialogue.
apps.loved: Daily questions organized by theme, a widget counting down to the next meeting, and the ability to see whether your answers matched your partner's.
apps.weak: In the free version only one topic from each category is available, and some questions feel AI-generated rather than written by people.
apps.whoFor: Long-distance couples or those who want to structure communication and learn more about each other.

apps.title: Lasting: Marriage & Couples
apps.verdict: Structured exercises based on proven methods start conversations about painful topics and help couples make real progress.
apps.loved: The exercises prompt conversation about painful topics without blame. Couples with very different histories report progress within the first sessions. One subscription works for both partners.
apps.weak: Content is oriented toward heterosexual couples in crisis. LGBTQ users and couples without acute conflict feel the format is not for them.
apps.whoFor: Couples in crisis who want to work on their relationship without a third party, especially those who cannot afford regular therapy.

apps.title: My Love-Relationship Countdown
apps.verdict: A relationship timer precise to the second, with password protection and date reminders. The widget freezes and shows outdated data.
apps.loved: A counter with seconds and the ability to lock the app with a fingerprint, valued as a private space for the couple.
apps.weak: The home-screen widget periodically freezes and shows the wrong date. Data is not restored after reinstalling without an account.
apps.whoFor: Couples who treasure their dates and want to see their relationship's length visually, especially those in long-distance relationships.

apps.title: Cougar Dating App - CougarD
apps.verdict: A niche platform for older women and younger men with video verification that genuinely reduces fakes, but the audience is small and geographically uneven.
apps.loved: Profile verification through photos and videos is noticed by users as genuinely reducing the number of fakes. Older women comment on the maturity of the audience.
apps.weak: The audience is very small and concentrated in a few regions. Profiles written in promotional language raise questions about authenticity.
apps.whoFor: Men attracted to older women and women 40+ looking for a younger partner, willing to accept a niche rather than mass audience.

quotes.text: CougarD stands out because it's built for women like me who want control. At 52, divorced and thriving, I refuse to waste time on flaky apps. 100% profile verification (especially female video checks) means almost no fakes-huge relief after

apps.title: SDC Adult Dating
apps.verdict: SDC is the only app in this set where a meaningful share of users report real meetings and a live community. Strict verification is mentioned as a genuine barrier to bots. The platform serves a specific swinger and lifestyle community, and for that audience it performs noticeably better than its competitors. The design is dated and prices are high, but the core product is real people.
apps.loved: Users point to verification that genuinely filters out bots, as well as links to offline events and clubs. Several people describe specific meetings and connections they built.
apps.weak: The interface is archaic and full access is expensive. Feed content is unfiltered: strangers' birthdays and irrelevant posts clutter it.
apps.whoFor: Couples and singles familiar with the lifestyle community (swinging, open relationships), especially those who have already been to themed club nights. Not for those who are just exploring.

apps.title: Holy — Christian Dating App
apps.verdict: The only app with manual review of every profile before approval, which sharply reduces fakes. Real wedding stories appear more often than average.
apps.loved: Manual profile checking cuts out most bots and scammers. You can see who showed interest without an extra fee. A small live team fixes errors on request.
apps.weak: Very few users outside the US and large Christian communities. Waiting for profile approval can take days. Age filters work inconsistently.
apps.whoFor: Practicing Christians for whom shared faith is a non-negotiable condition for a relationship.

quotes.text: Update: We got married last weekend! Only dated for 10 months. Thanks again Holy for helping me find my spouse. after being on dating apps for 6 months I found my person. We've dated from June until now and he proposed last week. I felt i

apps.title: Badoo Dating: Meet New People
apps.verdict: Basic messaging is available without a paid plan and video verification reduces the share of fakes, but most active profiles come from other countries with faked locations.
apps.loved: Video and photo verification reduces the number of obvious fakes. You can communicate without an extra plan. The audience is diverse.
apps.weak: Most active profiles are from distant countries with fake locations. Crypto-scheme scammers appear regularly. The same profiles keep cycling around.
apps.whoFor: Those willing to filter patiently and comfortable with international conversations. Not suitable for people who strictly want local matches.

quotes.text: It was good before as a free app for the most part. You just had to deal with the not legit fake people. Now may 2026 for about a year now I'm getting more then half of my match are people from outside the USA but there bio shows them livin

apps.title: Love Nudge
apps.verdict: An app built on Gary Chapman's five love languages: partners take a quiz, see each other's 'love tank' level, and receive tasks. A useful tool for intentional couples, but the interface needs work and some tasks feel generic.
apps.loved: Real-time visualization of a partner's satisfaction level and targeted reminders about specific actions help couples where one or both forget to show love in the right way.
apps.weak: The interface is unintuitive: you cannot create goals for your partner, notifications disappear, and completed tasks are not saved. The language of some questions is oriented toward religious and heterosexual couples, which puts off part of the audience.
apps.whoFor: Established couples who want to work on their relationship intentionally and understand the love language concept.

apps.title: DOWN: The Casual Dating App
apps.verdict: An honest casual-dating app with a small but relatively live audience. Fewer bots than competitors. users genuinely note this. The main weakness is the small reach in most cities, profiles run out quickly. Distance filters work poorly and the minimum search radius is too large. Real offline meetings do happen, which sets the app apart from most alternatives.
apps.loved: Relatively fewer bots than on comparable apps. Users' direct intentions are clear from the first glance. Real meetings happen. several users confirm this.
apps.weak: The audience runs out quickly in smaller cities. The minimum search radius is too large (60 miles). There is no activity indicator on profiles, so it is unclear who is actually online.
apps.whoFor: People in large cities looking for direct, low-commitment contact. In smaller towns the app is practically useless.

apps.title: Yubo: Chat Meet & Make Friends
apps.verdict: A young, active audience with interest tags and live streams, but most incoming friend requests are from bots, and finding a real conversation requires filtering.
apps.loved: Interest tags genuinely help find people with shared hobbies. Live streams create a sense of presence. Real friendships form.
apps.weak: Most incoming friend requests are from bots. Aggressive moderation bans users for harmless words in their bio. Live streaming features are unstable.
apps.whoFor: Ages 18 to 25 looking for friends or light social interaction, willing to pay.

apps.title: Boo — Dating. Friends. Chat.
apps.verdict: An app with an unusual idea: matchmaking based on personality types. Real users appreciate the atmosphere. It feels less superficial than competitors, and people willing to talk by interest do turn up. The problem is scale: in most regions the audience is tiny, matches arrive from other countries rather than nearby, and bots from third countries appear. Actual dates are rare. The app works more as an online social space.
apps.loved: The personality-type matching mechanic feels genuine. The atmosphere is kinder and more human than on Tinder or Hinge. The social tab with interest groups provides a place to talk beyond direct matching.
apps.weak: A small live audience in most cities. Bots and accounts from distant countries clutter the feed. Real meetings almost never happen even after months of chatting.
apps.whoFor: Introverts and personality-type enthusiasts open to online friendship without rushing toward an offline date. A poor fit for anyone looking for a partner in a specific city.

quotes.text: I have been using this app for a long time and although I have matched with people I have yet to actually meet anyone. If you are interested in online friends than this app is for you. There are many male and female users that post and inte

I didn't expect much when I first downloaded Boo, but it turned out to be one of the most refreshing social apps I've used. What immediately stood out was how different it felt compared to typical dating apps. Instead of focusing only on ap

apps.title: Zoe: Lesbian Dating & Chat
apps.verdict: Positioned as a space for women who love women, with manual moderation and an active support team. It genuinely works in large cities with an LGBTQ audience. The main problem is a significant number of scam profiles and men who pass verification.
apps.loved: A live support team that responds in chat, not a bot. A user-friendly interface and the ability to report a profile directly from the card. Some users note higher-quality profiles compared to general apps.
apps.weak: A significant share of profiles are scammers running bitcoin or military romance schemes. Men pass verification and stay in the feed. In smaller cities there are almost no active users.
apps.whoFor: Lesbian and bisexual women in large cities who value at least some moderation.

quotes.text: Assume everyone on this app is a scammer regardless if their profile is verified. They also have secondary verification which they CANNOT fake. This is not to say everyone on the app is a scammer, but a good majority of them are - easily fi

apps.title: Hinge Dating App: Match & Date
apps.verdict: The best profile format among swipe apps, but mass arbitrary bans and a rough HingeX algorithm spoil the experience.
apps.loved: Structured profiles with prompts make it easier to start a conversation. Real people do appear.
apps.weak: Random permanent bans without explanation. Geolocation works inaccurately.
apps.whoFor: People looking for a relationship who are willing to invest time in their profile.

quotes.text: Hinge is a nice app to consider, but please don't ever upgrade to HingeX. Something about HingeX and their algorithm there feels so unethical. My first few months on Hinge+, I was getting a steady number of likes a day, seeing many sugges

apps.title: Meetup: Social Events & Groups
apps.verdict: A unique concept for meeting people through shared activities and live events, which has degraded after a change of ownership toward aggressive monetization.
apps.loved: Live meetups around shared interests produce organic connections that no swipe format can match. The range of groups and events is wide.
apps.weak: Basic event search and the attendee list are locked behind a paid plan. Automated bans happen without human review. The interface became confusing after recent updates.
apps.whoFor: People who have moved to a new city or are looking for a community around shared interests rather than direct romance.

apps.title: BBW Dating & Curvy Meet: Bustr
apps.verdict: A niche dating app for plus-size people and those attracted to them. Real users note the absence of any audience in smaller cities, bots simulating interest immediately after sign-up, and aggressive messages from men. Some success stories look credible, but the audience is small.
apps.loved: The niche focus reduces the feeling of being judged on appearance. Plus-size women say they feel desired without qualifications for the first time. Body-type and interest filters work.
apps.weak: Live audience is thin: outside large cities finding a real nearby person is nearly impossible. Waves of 'likes' arrive from accounts that then go silent.
apps.whoFor: Plus-size women and men attracted to the BBW format who are willing to accept a small active base in exchange for a niche community.

quotes.text: I weigh around 300 pounds (5'8", probably a size 23) and I just got married two weeks ago to my partner of 4 years. We met through the app. She loved me at 220 pounds and she loved me at 300 pounds. I'm probably the heaviest guy she's ever

apps.title: Mutual LDS Dating: Meet & Date
apps.verdict: A niche app for single members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints with real success stories, but outside Utah the audience is very thin and the algorithm ignores the set radius.
apps.loved: Shared values and level of church involvement are listed directly on the profile, shortening the path to compatible people.
apps.weak: Outside Utah and large LDS communities the app is essentially empty. Inactive church members and people from other faiths appear in the feed.
apps.whoFor: Practicing members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints living in areas with a dense Mormon community.

quotes.text: If the intent of the creators is solely to create a frustrating experience that will drive users either off the app or to pay them money, it works. Notes from a male user: They show your profile to an extremely limited number of people un

I swipe up probably less than 1% of the time. I'll spend 45 minutes of my free time just swiping down. Takes FOREVER to come across someone that's decent looking. Paid for one month. No more. I'll literally swipe down through all of the ava

apps.title: Feeld: Dating for the Curious
apps.verdict: Feeld occupies a unique niche for polyamorous and kink-oriented people and still has no real alternative. The main problem is not audience quality but chronic technical instability: the app is considered genuinely buggy even by loyal users. Outside large cities the user base is nearly empty.
apps.loved: An open and inclusive atmosphere where there is no need to explain a non-traditional lifestyle. The ability to create a joint profile with a partner attracts couples looking for a third or other partners. When people are present, their quality is noted as high.
apps.weak: Chronic technical failures: messages disappear, notifications are phantom, accounts break without warning. The user base is small and inactive outside a few major cities. Moderation bans without explanation and with no appeal process.
apps.whoFor: Polyamorous couples and singles, as well as people with kink interests, who live in large cities and are willing to put up with unstable technical performance for lack of alternatives.

apps.title: Bumpy – International Dating
apps.verdict: International search with country filters and a built-in translator works, and some users have found partners, but waves of off-target likes undermine trust.
apps.loved: Country filters let users target people from specific regions with purpose. The built-in translator and time-zone display simplify communication across borders.
apps.weak: Suspicious waves of thousands of likes from off-target regions. Profile visibility drops sharply after paying. Scammers use video calls for extortion.
apps.whoFor: People deliberately looking for a partner from a specific country and willing to carefully vet every contact.

quotes.text: I paid for a premium subscription twice to support the app and access full features. During both subscriptions, engagement on my profile was great until the final 2 days of my subscription — in one case, only 2 likes over two days. Which wa

apps.title: Dil Mil: South Asian Dating
apps.verdict: Niche matching for the South Asian diaspora with real success stories, but the algorithm keeps showing profiles hundreds of miles away, archives conversations without warning, and fails to clean out scammers. The core of the product works. The wrapper does not.
apps.loved: Several users found life partners here. Filters for culture, religion, diet, and family values make matches more meaningful than on universal apps.
apps.weak: The algorithm cycles through the same profiles repeatedly without regard to distance. The archive feature kills live conversations. Fake profiles and scammers appear regularly, and moderation is slow to react.
apps.whoFor: Members of the South Asian diaspora who care about cultural and family compatibility and are willing to tolerate technical inconveniences.

quotes.text: I cannot recommend the DilMil app highly enough! After using it for a while, I met my fiancé through this incredible platform. The app's user-friendly interface and customizable options made the whole process enjoyable and effortless. One o

apps.title: 3Fun: Couples & Singles Dating
apps.verdict: An app for open relationships and threesomes with an interesting joint-profile mechanic for couples. In practice it suffers from a critically small audience outside large cities. Most profiles within a 100-km radius have been inactive for months. Single men massively create fake couple profiles. Safety for women raises serious concerns: complaints about aggressive behavior get no response from moderation.
apps.loved: The joint couple profile mechanic is convenient. Group chats work. For those living in a large city and prepared for a long search, real meetings do occasionally happen.
apps.weak: Dead audience in most regions. Single men pose as couples. Women's safety is not ensured by moderation. Verification does not protect against stolen photos.
apps.whoFor: Couples in large cities who are already familiar with this relationship format and prepared for a long search. Not suitable for singles or residents of smaller cities.

apps.title: Adam4Adam Gay Dating Chat A4A
apps.verdict: A large established gay user base with accessible features, but bots and scammers attack on every first contact and support does not respond.
apps.loved: A large gay audience including in regions where niche apps are empty. Many features available without an extra plan.
apps.weak: Bots and scammers redirect to Snapchat or Telegram on every first contact. Support does not respond to complaints. Trans women receive unjustified blocks.
apps.whoFor: Gay and bisexual men with experience on these platforms who can quickly spot scammers, especially in cities with a small audience for specialized apps.

apps.title: Relatio: Couples Relationship
apps.verdict: Structured couple exercises with five-minute sessions genuinely help with difficult conversations. Better suited for couples in crisis than for those who are doing well.
apps.loved: Several men report real progress working through the pelvic-floor exercise program and anxiety management. The 30-day structure gives a sense of a journey.
apps.weak: Hidden auto-renewal without clear notification is the top complaint. Content repeats and is not personalized despite promises. Videos often fail to play.
apps.whoFor: Couples or men looking for basic exercises and relationship advice who read subscription terms carefully. Not for those expecting personalized or professional support.

apps.title: OkCupid Dating: Date Singles
apps.verdict: OkCupid retains its extended profiles and compatibility questions, but has turned into a platform for foreign scammers. Most incoming likes come from the Philippines and Nigeria with faked locations. The algorithm has degraded since the Match Group acquisition.
apps.loved: Detailed profiles and compatibility questions help those who seek them. Support for non-traditional relationship formats is present.
apps.weak: Foreign profiles with faked locations flood the feed. Matches disappear and real local people are nearly absent.
apps.whoFor: Users in large cities who value profile depth and are willing to filter through a lot of noise.

quotes.text: UPDATED 4-22-2026 this app has literally been inundated with thousands of fake profiles within the last 24 hours! It's a joke, it's so obvious to see these fake profiles where all the people look like they are models and yet Match Group do

apps.title: PURE: Open-Minded Dating App
apps.verdict: Pure offers a direct approach to casual encounters without long conversations, and the idea resonates with the target audience. The real problem is that few people are around in most cities, and aggressive AI moderation bans real users as often as it bans rule-breakers. Those who do find a match often reach a real meeting.
apps.loved: The directness of the format: a profile lives for 24 hours, which filters out passive users. Conversation quality is higher than on standard dating apps because both parties' intentions are clear upfront. Verification is present.
apps.weak: The user base is small in many cities, making it hard to find someone nearby at the right moment. Moderation bans without warning or appeal, causing sharp frustration even among loyal paying users.
apps.whoFor: Adults looking for no-strings encounters in cities with sufficient user density. Not suitable for those who want to build up communication before meeting.

apps.title: Casual Dating & Flirt - Kasual
apps.verdict: The flip mechanic is liked by those who have tried it, but active users are nearly absent outside a few cities.
apps.loved: The full profile is visible before choosing, which appeals to people who want to know someone before deciding. The rare real matches lead to pleasant conversations.
apps.weak: Catastrophically few active users outside a handful of cities. Escort accounts and dead profiles outnumber real users.
apps.whoFor: Residents of large US cities open to experimenting with a different dating format. Not suitable for small towns or regions with low user density.

apps.title: 3way: Couples & Singles Dating
apps.verdict: A niche service for couples and singles looking for non-standard relationship formats. The concept attracts its audience, but real users are scarce: many profiles disappear within a day and people vanish after first contact. Real meetings are rare.
apps.loved: A variety of relationship formats and an open, non-judgmental atmosphere. Some users note easy onboarding and quick initial matches after signing up.
apps.weak: Few active users locally. Most profiles shown are from other states or countries. Fakes and bots are unfiltered and moderation does not function. Blocked profiles reappear.
apps.whoFor: Couples and singles open to non-standard relationship formats, primarily in large US cities.

apps.title: HER:Lesbian&Queer LGBTQ Dating
apps.verdict: HER solves a real problem: lesbian and queer women need a space without cis men, and HER was long the only option. But the platform is flooded with scam networks, bots, and men bypassing filters. Moderation cannot keep up with the flow of fakes, and bugs make daily use of the app unstable.
apps.loved: A unique queer women's community where you can openly state identity and preferences. Some users find real relationships here precisely because the audience is targeted.
apps.whoFor: Lesbians, bisexual, and queer women who want a specialized platform and are prepared to carefully filter incoming contacts.

apps.title: 3Somer: Couples Dating App
apps.verdict: A niche service for couples and singles looking for swinging encounters. Dead audience in most cities. A real couple from Los Angeles reports no mutual matches after a month. No distance filter. Profiles with obvious signs of being fake use stolen photos. The app does not let you delete your account after signing up.
apps.loved: The focus on swinging culture and threesomes meets a real demand from an audience that has nowhere to look on mainstream apps. Several couples describe real meetings.
apps.weak: Dead audience in most cities. No distance filter. Fake profiles with templated money offers. Account deletion is impossible. Several complaints about charges continuing after deleting the app.
apps.whoFor: Couples and singles open to swinging in large cities with a dense audience. Almost no chance in smaller cities.

apps.title: Bumble Dating App: Meet & Date
apps.verdict: The algorithm is built to retain users, not to produce matches. Profiles go unanswered, dead matches accumulate, and moderation does not respond to threats.
apps.loved: Women who write first have sometimes found real people and built conversations. The first-move mechanic reduces pressure on men.
apps.weak: Dead conversations with no replies. Shadow bans without warning. Complaints about threats of violence left without response from support.
apps.whoFor: Women willing to write first and accept low activity.

quotes.text: I have used Bumble off and on over the years, but it just gets worse and worse. When you do match with people, they never respond. I realize this is a problem amongst all apps; however, it seems to be a particular problem on this platform.

So I have recently deleted bumble because I wasn't getting literally anything. No interaction from any woman. No likes, no messages or responses. Now that's not the only reason I deleted it. After the second month, I started getting only 3

apps.title: Chispa: Dating App for Latinos
apps.verdict: An app for the Latino audience with a serious quality problem: many fakes and inactive profiles, distance filters that do not work, and an algorithm that deliberately suppresses organic matches. Real meeting stories exist but are rare.
apps.loved: The rare couples who did find a partner through Chispa mention the niche focus on Latinos.
apps.weak: Fake likes to provoke purchases. Dead and unverified profiles. Distance filters are ignored.
apps.whoFor: Latinos willing to sift through a lot of noise in search of real people.

quotes.text: You keep sending me all these slogans and phrases a few times a day, what is the good of that??? How bout sending me sum MATCHES?? All these dating apps are so flawed, problem is women get 100's of endless messages, while men get basically

apps.title: Wild: Adult Casual Dating App
apps.verdict: Wild is positioned as a casual-encounters app, and a small share of users do find real contacts. However, the live user base is thin and geographically uneven: in rural areas and small cities there is practically no one. Bots and fakes are present but do not dominate the way they do in Mingle2 or Ashley Madison.
apps.loved: The private-photo feature, which lets users share selectively, is appreciated by those who value control over personal data. Some users note that people here state their intentions honestly, which simplifies communication.
apps.weak: The active audience is concentrated in a few cities. Elsewhere it is mostly inactive or long-outdated profiles. Bots appear often enough to be an inconvenience.
apps.whoFor: Residents of large cities looking for no-strings encounters. Not suitable for people outside major urban areas or those wanting to build up a conversation before meeting.

apps.title: Curvy Dating App: WooPlus
apps.verdict: The plus-size dating app is positioned as a community but in practice has become a venue for scammers, adult-content sellers, and beauty contests with cash prizes. Real couples are rare and moderation is weak.
apps.loved: The 'moments' feature (photo posts) gives a quick feeling of attention. A few users genuinely found partners, including one woman who found her husband after several years of use.
apps.weak: Scammers and bots in every second conversation by users' own accounts. Cash-prize contests turned the feed into a beauty competition rather than a dating space. Moderation does not respond to complaints.
apps.whoFor: Plus-size women with a high tolerance for noise and a willingness to personally verify every contact's authenticity.

quotes.text: There's been three separate occasions in which I've downloaded this app and then later deleted it. Most of the reason behind that is how much sexual harassment I receive from men on the app. No matter how many times I report someone, how sp

apps.title: BlackGentry: Black Dating App
apps.verdict: The app is positioned as an exclusive club for Black professionals with manual profile review. According to reviews, the screening barely works: the crowd is no different from mainstream apps, fakes pass verification, and the algorithm ignores age and distance settings.
apps.loved: The existence of a space oriented toward Black users is valued by those who felt underrepresented on universal platforms. A few people found quality matches.
apps.weak: The claimed 'screening' is not felt in practice. Men in their 20s appear for women who specified ages 35 to 45. Most likes are hidden behind a $30-per-month paywall. Fake profiles pass photo verification.
apps.whoFor: Black singles willing to pay for a theoretically higher-quality audience. Works better in large cities with a high user density.

apps.title: 3Woo: Couples & Singles Dating
apps.verdict: The polyamorous and swinging niche is in demand, but the audience is concentrated in one location and the algorithm apparently hides mutual matches.
apps.loved: Several users noted that profiles look more real than in other niche apps. Some couples found live matches.

apps.title: Waplog - Dating & Video Call
apps.verdict: The app promotes itself as a video-call dating platform, but the real audience has been replaced by scammers. Users describe universal fakes, photo extortion, bitcoin schemes, and redirection to Telegram. Anyone looking for a real person has no business here.
apps.loved: The idea of video-based meetings with people from other countries sounds appealing, and a few users found long-term relationships years ago when the platform was just launching.
apps.weak: Practically all conversation partners are bots or scammers. The video chat is used mainly for sexual shows rather than dating. Accounts get blocked without explanation.
apps.whoFor: No one looking for a real partner. Historically attracted people interested in international socializing, but that niche has long been taken over by scammers.

apps.title: Flirtini - Match, Chat, Flirt
apps.verdict: Small audience. Most incoming contacts are bots with identical scripts. Almost no real people even in large cities.
apps.loved: Conversation partners at least send a rejection rather than going silent, which is noticeable compared to other apps.
apps.weak: Bots with the same photos under different names make up most contacts. The account cannot be deleted without contacting support. People from other cities dominate.

apps.title: Mamba: Dating, Meet New People
apps.verdict: The app is overrun by scammers and fakes. Users have run experiments: they wrote to dozens of profiles and all turned out to be scammers. Even verified accounts are fake. Profile locations are constantly faked. Moderation does not respond to complaints.
apps.loved: Platform veterans note the large profile base and the ability to find a Russian-speaking audience. A handful of users report real meetings and long-term relationships.
apps.weak: Near-total domination of fakes and bots, including verified accounts. Scammers follow scripts, quickly move to Telegram, and demand money or data. Support ignores complaints.
apps.whoFor: Practically no one. Historically for the Russian-speaking diaspora, but today the audience has been replaced by scammers.

apps.title: FilipinoCupid: Filipino Dating
apps.verdict: A dating app targeting a Filipino audience, completely overrun by scammers. Literally every second review describes the same scheme: first message 'hello/hi handsome', then a move to WhatsApp or Telegram, then a request for money. Photos are easily identified as stolen via reverse image search.
apps.loved: Almost nothing. A handful of users mention that some real profiles do appear, but they are hard to find.
apps.weak: The app is dominated by scammers from Nigeria and other countries using stolen photos. No profile verification. Support does not respond to complaints. Reported accounts continue operating.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended in its current state.

apps.title: Waiter: find love by AI
apps.verdict: The concept of patient algorithmic matchmaking is appealing, but nearly no one among the reviewers has received a single real match over the entire period of use.
apps.loved: The no-infinite-scroll matching concept and the interest-question algorithm receive praise even in scathing reviews.
apps.weak: Not one confirmed real match among hundreds of reviews. Profiles look fake or pulled from external sites. Match notifications are used as a trap.
apps.whoFor: No one. Even those willing to pay for a more thoughtful approach to dating will get nothing this product promises.

apps.title: Aisle - Indian Dating App
apps.verdict: The app is positioned as a serious service for the Indian diaspora, but the audience has been taken over by scammers. Blackmail and sextortion through video calls after matches have been documented. Real active users are nearly absent: out of hundreds of profiles, people report finding no one who had opened the app within the past week. Verification is claimed but does not protect against fake accounts.
apps.loved: The concept of the only niche service for educated Indian diaspora members oriented toward serious relationships. One user noted the team helped restore an account when changing a phone number.
apps.weak: Fake profiles and scammers make up most of the active audience. Blackmail schemes through video calls have been documented. Dead audience outside India. Match alerts for new users are absent.
apps.whoFor: Possibly suitable for residents of large Indian cities willing to carefully verify every contact and never move to a third-party messenger.

apps.title: DateMyAge™ - Mature Dating 40+
apps.verdict: The same mechanic as Dating.com: a flood of fake messages immediately after sign-up and a charge per letter with no path to a real meeting.
apps.loved: The concept of an app for mature dating resonates. The 40+ audience is genuinely looking for such a product.
apps.weak: Mass fake profiles including accounts that overlap with Dating.com. Operators simulate real people. Credits are charged for every action on top of the base plan.

apps.title: EZMatch: 18+ Dating,Meet&Flirt
apps.loved: Almost nothing real by the criteria of a live audience.
apps.weak: All incoming messages are from bots or scammers. Banners interrupt every action. Account verification is nonexistent.

apps.title: Meete - Meet New Friends
apps.verdict: The app is built on an asymmetric model: men pay gems per message, women allegedly receive money for chatting. In practice most conversation partners are bots. Real connections almost never form. Money drains quickly.
apps.loved: The 'social dating with monetization' concept initially attracts some women with small early payouts. The interface is simple and navigation is intuitive for new users.
apps.weak: Bots flood the feed from the first minute of sign-up. Men spend significant sums without realizing they are not talking to real people. Women report payouts stopping after the first withdrawal.
apps.whoFor: Formally for dating and socializing. In practice the product does not work as intended.

apps.title: Dating.com: Global Chat & Date
apps.verdict: Hired operators or bots carry on conversations with paying users, simulating real interest. No conversation partner ever agrees to communicate outside the platform.
apps.loved: Beautiful profiles and an international audience for those looking for long-distance connections. The interface is described as pleasant.
apps.weak: Operators pretend to be real users and refuse to communicate outside the app. Conversations are deliberately cut off to prompt credit purchases.
apps.whoFor: No one. This is not a dating service in any practical sense.

apps.title: Once: Perfect Match Dating App
apps.verdict: The app works on a scheme: AI characters lure users into conversations then block replies without purchasing 'diamonds'. Real users are rare. According to reviews this is not a dating service but monetization of the illusion of connection.
apps.loved: The idea of 'one algorithm-chosen match per day' appeals to those who want more intentional dating. The interface is clean and visually pleasant.
apps.weak: Virtually all active profiles are AI bots. Real conversation with a live person is practically unachievable without significant spending on in-app currency.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended in its current state.
